roadmapMeta.title: Silicon Quest
roadmapMeta.northStar: Become a hardware-aware performance engineer who designs, measures and optimizes low-level systems across CPUs, NVIDIA GPUs and FPGAs.
roadmapMeta.moduleNotice: Provisional topic modules derived from the roadmap, not verified textbook chapters. Selective study supports projects; completing every book is not required.
roadmapMeta.seedProgress: No milestone is marked complete without implementation evidence.

budget.note: Historical planning assumptions; excludes tax, commercial books and board/workstation costs. Recheck official prices before purchasing.

hardwareNotes: Apple Silicon supports local C++/Python experiments; native CUDA requires a compatible NVIDIA environment.
Verify supported x86-64 Linux/Windows Vivado/Vitis/PYNQ versions and board files.
PYNQ-Z2 is for compact networks; resize based on actual synthesis.
Verify hls4ml support; modern FINN does not officially target PYNQ-Z2 in this roadmap.
firstMonth: Week 1: CMake/CTest, compiler/sanitizers, microbenchmark; binary arithmetic and counter testbench.
Week 2: AoS/SoA and sequential/random experiments; FSM and 8-bit ALU simulation.
Week 3: allocation, branch prediction and data movement; fixed-point MAC simulation.
Week 4: technical note with graphs/tests/limitations; engine correctness contract and dated CUDA/FPGA access plan.

books.title: Computer Systems: A Programmer’s Perspective
books.focus: Memory, linking, caches, processes, performance foundations

books.title: Digital Design and Computer Architecture: ARM Edition
Parallel Programming for FPGAs
books.focus: HLS, pipelining, memory and hardware optimizations

books.title: Efficient Processing of Deep Neural Networks

phases.title: C++ / systems foundations
phases.focus: Modern C++, Linux, memory, profiling; begin digital design
phases.exitCriteria: Explain CPU timing differences with evidence and simulate a basic register/ALU/FSM.
phases.parallelTrack: 1–2 hours/week: binary arithmetic, combinational/sequential logic, testbenches, counters and state machines.

phases.title: Low-latency C++
phases.focus: CPU optimization, concurrent systems, processor architecture
phases.exitCriteria: Correct engine, controlled workload, p50/p95/p99, throughput, hardware/compiler config and writeup.
phases.parallelTrack: Pipeline registers, fixed-point MAC, reset/clock semantics and simulation coverage.

phases.title: CUDA & GPU architecture
phases.focus: CUDA programming, GPU architecture and profiling
phases.exitCriteria: Correct reproducible kernel suite, measured optimizations and technical report.
phases.parallelTrack: Synthesis flow, BRAM/DSP, timing constraints and a simulated pipelined MAC.

phases.title: Inference systems & quantization
phases.focus: GPU serving, runtime design and quantization
phases.exitCriteria: Working published runtime, profiler results and fair baseline comparisons.
phases.parallelTrack: Zynq PS/PL, AXI4-Lite/Stream, DMA, buffering and PYNQ overlays.

phases.title: FPGA implementation fundamentals
phases.focus: Concentrated implementation of the single FPGA capstone
phases.exitCriteria: Working physical-board DMA/control and verified arithmetic pipeline with timing/utilization reports.

phases.title: Quantized CPU / GPU / FPGA accelerator
phases.focus: Deploy the compact IMU gesture classifier and compare platforms
phases.exitCriteria: Physical board demo, bitstream/driver source, correctness, synthesis/timing and CPU/GPU/FPGA report.

phases.title: Polish, architecture depth & recruiting
phases.focus: Reproducibility, writeups, demonstrations, selected credentials and portfolio
phases.exitCriteria: Four articles, reproducible repositories, demonstrations and evidence-based interview stories.

projects.title: Low-Latency Matching Engine
projects.summary: A correct limit-order-book / matching engine with controlled optimization experiments.
milestones: Add, cancel, execute and optionally modify orders
Deterministic replay against a slower reference
Controlled workloads with throughput and tail latency
At least three optimization investigations, retaining negative results
projects.definitionOfDone: Tests, reproducible workload, p50/p95/p99, hardware/compiler configuration and profiler-backed optimization report.

projects.title: CUDA KernelForge
projects.summary: A CUDA kernel library and reproducible benchmark suite.
milestones: Vector addition, reduction and prefix scan
Naive and shared-memory tiled GEMM
Convolution or related compute-heavy kernel
Meaningful optimized CPU and NVIDIA library baselines
Nsight experiments and technical report
projects.definitionOfDone: Correct kernels, controlled reproducible benchmarks, optimized baselines and measured explanations.

projects.title: GPU Inference Runtime
projects.summary: A C++ / CUDA / TensorRT inference service for a small supported model.
milestones: Reference model accuracy and latency
Compatible C++ TensorRT runtime
Custom CUDA preprocessing
Batching, streams and transfer-overlap experiments
Throughput/latency curves and precision accuracy evaluation
projects.definitionOfDone: Working end-to-end runtime, correctness tests, profiler evidence and fair loaded-system comparisons.

projects.title: PYNQ Quantized Accelerator
projects.summary: One integrated PYNQ-Z2 capstone: verified RTL/HLS building blocks through compact quantized IMU inference.
milestones: Simulate 8-bit ALU and fixed-point MAC
Synthesize pipelined dot product and fixed-point FIR/preprocessor
Physical AXI/DMA round trip against C++ reference
Collect leakage-free train/validation/test data and train FP32 model
Quantize INT8 and build equivalent CPU/CUDA baselines
Fit and deploy a supported FPGA implementation
Separate compute, transfer and end-to-end measurements
Optional runtime-loaded weights after the baseline fits
projects.definitionOfDone: Physical board demo, source/driver/bitstream, correctness tests, resource/timing reports and fair CPU/GPU/FPGA benchmarks. Runtime-loaded weights and double buffering are optional.

credentials.title: Fundamentals of Accelerated Computing With Modern CUDA C/C++
credentials.description: Approximately 8 hours; competency credential requires satisfying course assessment requirements.
credentials.budgetNote: US$90 in the May 2026 PDF; availability, assessment and checkout price must be rechecked.

credentials.title: FPGA Design for Embedded Systems Specialization
credentials.description: University-issued completion certificate, not an AMD professional certificate. Some material uses Intel/Quartus/Nios II; transfer fundamentals to AMD/PYNQ.
credentials.budgetNote: Planning assumption: US$59/month for 2–4 months (US$118–236); verify local pricing and eligibility.

credentials.title: NVIDIA Certified Associate — AI Infrastructure and Operations
credentials.description: Role-dependent GPU infrastructure/operations credential; less directly aligned with CUDA kernel development.
credentials.budgetNote: Earlier PDF: US$50 fundamentals + US$125 exam; verify current requirements and prices.

credentials.title: Additional CUDA / Nsight modules
credentials.description: C++ standard-library GPU acceleration/scaling; CUDA ML profiling; Nsight Systems pipelines; custom Python analysis scripts.
credentials.budgetNote: May 2026 PDF listed US$30 each, up to US$150 total. Verify current availability and pricing.

modules.title: Caches & locality
modules.summary: Connect working-set size and access pattern to measured CPU behavior.
modules.exercise: Benchmark sequential and random traversal over several array sizes.
modules.doneWhen: Correctness checks, raw repeated timings, hardware details and an explanation of the observed trend.

modules.title: AoS vs SoA
modules.summary: Explore how contiguous storage and layout change data movement.
modules.exercise: Implement equivalent AoS and SoA computations and benchmark them.
modules.doneWhen: Matching outputs and at least two controlled input sizes with raw timings.

modules.title: RAII & move semantics
modules.summary: Reason about C++20 object lifetime and ownership before measuring performance.
modules.exercise: Write a small resource-owning type and inspect copy/move behavior.
modules.doneWhen: Lifetime tests pass and ownership behavior is explained without claiming unmeasured speedups.

modules.title: Allocation strategies
modules.summary: Compare allocation choices using the same workload.
modules.exercise: Compare baseline allocation with a pool or reserved contiguous storage.
modules.doneWhen: Correct outputs, controlled inputs and repeated baseline/change measurements.

modules.title: Reliable microbenchmarks
modules.summary: Establish reproducible measurements before optimization.
modules.exercise: Build a C++ benchmark harness with a correctness test and raw result output.
modules.doneWhen: CMake/CTest workflow, warmup, repeat counts and reproducible benchmark invocation are documented.

modules.title: Processes & virtual memory
modules.summary: Build an OS-level explanation of memory behavior.
objectives: Distinguish process address spaces and physical memory
modules.exercise: Record a small process-memory experiment and relate observations to its access pattern.
modules.doneWhen: Test setup and observed results are recorded with clear limitations.

modules.title: Atomics & contention
modules.summary: Understand queues, ordering and shared cache lines.
modules.exercise: Implement a tested SPSC queue or contention experiment for the engine pipeline.
modules.doneWhen: Deterministic correctness evidence and a controlled contention benchmark are available.

modules.title: Matching-engine experiments
modules.summary: Optimize against a correct replayable engine baseline.
modules.exercise: Investigate at least three layout, allocation or queue changes.
modules.doneWhen: Reference validation, workload distributions, throughput/tail latency and a report include regressions.

modules.title: CUDA execution model
modules.summary: Map work to threads, warps and blocks.
modules.exercise: Implement vector addition with CPU reference validation.
modules.doneWhen: Correct output for boundary sizes and a reproducible GPU timing method.

modules.title: Coalescing & bandwidth
modules.summary: Measure data-access behavior and asynchronous transfer boundaries.
modules.exercise: Compare controlled GPU access patterns and capture Nsight evidence.
modules.doneWhen: Correctness, memory-traffic interpretation and repeatable measured results.

modules.title: Reduction & prefix scan
modules.summary: Practice parallel aggregation with explicit correctness checks.
modules.exercise: Implement reduction and parallel prefix scan for several input sizes.
modules.doneWhen: Reference checks including edge cases and performance measurements for both kernels.

modules.title: Tiled GEMM & convolution
modules.summary: Explore shared-memory tiling and relevant optimized baselines.
modules.exercise: Implement naive/tiled GEMM and one convolution or related compute-heavy kernel.
modules.doneWhen: Correct results, relevant CPU/library comparisons and profiler-backed discussion.

modules.title: Quantitative bottlenecks
modules.summary: Use measured workload behavior to study hardware limits.
modules.exercise: Explain a KernelForge bottleneck using measurements and architecture concepts.
modules.doneWhen: Profiler evidence supports the bottleneck claim and caveats are documented.

modules.title: Serving, streams & batching
modules.summary: Measure end-to-end inference under realistic load.
modules.exercise: Build the C++/TensorRT runtime with custom CUDA preprocessing where supported.
modules.doneWhen: Correct runtime plus throughput/latency curves across multiple load levels.

modules.title: Logic, counters & FSMs
modules.summary: Begin the FPGA track with simulation.
modules.exercise: Simulate a counter, FSM and 8-bit ALU.
modules.doneWhen: Corner-case checks pass; no physical bitstream is required at this stage.

modules.title: Fixed-point & pipelined MAC
modules.summary: Make numerical and pipeline behavior explicit.
modules.exercise: Model and simulate a fixed-point MAC with pipeline registers.
modules.doneWhen: Self-checking known vectors pass and reset/clock semantics are explained.

modules.title: Synthesis & timing reports
modules.summary: Connect RTL structure to hardware resource and timing constraints.
modules.exercise: Synthesize the pipelined MAC if compatible tools are available.
modules.doneWhen: Simulation evidence plus a synthesis report, or an explicit tooling blocker without invented results.

modules.title: HLS pipelining & partitioning
modules.summary: Compare hardware scheduling choices within the one capstone.
modules.exercise: Synthesize a pipelined dot product and compare one HLS scheduling change.
modules.doneWhen: Numerical checks and measured LUT/FF/DSP/BRAM, timing and II are recorded.

modules.title: Fixed-point FIR block
modules.summary: Build a small reusable arithmetic block for the capstone.
modules.exercise: Implement a fixed-point FIR or preprocessing block against a C++ reference.
modules.doneWhen: Known vectors pass and the role of the block in the capstone is documented.

modules.title: Zynq PS, PL & overlays
modules.summary: Understand the host/accelerator split and supported tool flow.
objectives: Distinguish processing system and programmable logic
modules.exercise: Survey compatible PYNQ-Z2 build/runtime versions and identify the development machine.
modules.doneWhen: A dated compatibility decision and tool-access plan exist.

modules.title: AXI, DMA & buffers
modules.summary: Move verified data between ARM and programmable logic.
modules.exercise: Load a supported overlay and round-trip known vectors through the data path.
modules.doneWhen: Physical PYNQ-Z2 output matches reference; core and transfer timing are separated.

modules.title: Quantization & accuracy
modules.summary: Measure precision changes against a held-out reference.
objectives: Record scales/zero points or fixed-point format
modules.exercise: Train FP32 and quantize the compact gesture classifier to INT8.
modules.doneWhen: Train/validation/test separation, FP32/INT8 metrics and confusion matrix are recorded.

modules.title: Fit-to-device inference
modules.summary: Deploy a compact network based on real synthesis constraints.
modules.exercise: Use a confirmed hls4ml flow or a small handwritten HLS datapath and deploy to PYNQ-Z2.
modules.doneWhen: Physical-board demo, design/driver source, accuracy, resource/timing and fair benchmark reports.

modules.title: Revisit measured bottlenecks
modules.summary: Choose deeper study using evidence from completed projects.
objectives: Connect pipelines and precision to results
modules.exercise: Write one focused architecture note linked to a real project bottleneck.
modules.doneWhen: The note cites project evidence, limitations and a testable next hypothesis.

quizQuestions.prompt: Which evidence best supports a performance improvement claim?
choices: One fastest run after editing the code
Correctness checks, a controlled baseline, repeated measurements and recorded configuration
A profiler screenshot without the input or hardware details
A larger input for only the optimized version

quizQuestions.prompt: Why might sequential traversal outperform random traversal of the same array?
choices: Sequential order guarantees every access hits L1
Random traversal always uses more arithmetic
Sequential access can improve locality and let prefetching anticipate future accesses
The compiler must remove all sequential loads

quizQuestions.prompt: What is the central idea of RAII?
choices: Tie resource ownership to object lifetime so destruction releases the resource
Move every object to avoid allocation
Use global variables for every resource
Manually release resources after every expression

quizQuestions.prompt: Why report p95/p99 as well as throughput?
choices: Percentiles eliminate all measurement noise
Throughput alone proves every request is fast
Tail percentiles measure source-code complexity
Aggregate throughput can hide slow requests in the latency distribution

quizQuestions.prompt: Which adjacent-thread access pattern is generally favorable for coalescing?
choices: Each thread accesses an unrelated allocation
Adjacent threads access adjacent suitably aligned elements
Every thread serially reads the full input
Every warp uses a different numerical precision

quizQuestions.prompt: A pipeline has latency 5 cycles and initiation interval 1. What does that imply?
choices: Every result takes only 1 cycle from input
Only one input may enter every 5 cycles
It can accept a new input each cycle, with each result emerging 5 cycles later
Its clock frequency is exactly 5 GHz

quizQuestions.prompt: What is needed for a fair FPGA latency report?
choices: Report core compute and data-transfer/end-to-end timing separately
Report only the HLS estimated cycle count as host latency
Exclude all numerical checks
Assume DMA has zero overhead

quizQuestions.prompt: After quantizing a model to INT8, what should be checked?
choices: Only that the output tensor exists
Only that the model file is smaller
Training accuracy on the same data used to tune quantization
Held-out accuracy, numerical conventions, resource use and measured performance

measurementRules: Establish correctness against a reference before optimizing.
Pin input sizes, seeds, model versions, precision, compiler flags and hardware.
Separate setup, transfer, compute and end-to-end response time.
Warm up appropriately; repeat measurements and report distribution/variance.
Use fair optimized CPU and relevant GPU-library baselines.
Separate FPGA pipeline latency from ARM/host/DMA overhead.
Report numerical accuracy and resource/energy methodology when changing precision.
Retain failed or regressing experiments with explanations.
Store scripts and raw benchmark data with charts.
